- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast increase to +2–4% above peak.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model fails to adjust; apply “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.33 after 7 days, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact to recent auctions; use “event dampening” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per event beyond 15.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; if forecast is >75% above 18d mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
